synopsis: Qwen-VL turns a language model into a multilingual image-understanding system through a visual encoder, a position-aware compression adapter, and three training stages. It produces captions, answers and textual bounding boxes. Strong generalist benchmark results coexist with specialist gaps and limited causal evidence for individual design choices.

problem.text: The authors target coarse visual understanding in open LVLMs: useful assistants must read text and identify specific regions, as well as describe whole images. Qwen-VL combines these tasks within a shared image-and-language interface.

contributions.text: A position-aware adapter connects OpenCLIP ViT-bigG to Qwen-7B, keeping the visual sequence entering the language model at 256 features.
A staged curriculum combines large-scale bilingual image-text alignment, seven-task pre-training and dialogue tuning; bounding boxes are learned as ordinary text with structural delimiters.
The authors report broad improvements over compared generalist models, but their tables retain exceptions and stronger specialist results.

inputs: Resized images interleaved with text prompts or dialogue
Optional referring expressions or textual region coordinates
outputs: Referring expressions and normalized bounding-box strings; OCR training also uses quadrilateral strings

steps.name: Encode and preserve location
steps.detail: ViT-bigG, initialized from OpenCLIP, extracts stride-14 patch features. A randomly initialized single-layer cross-attention adapter uses learnable queries and image-feature keys; 2D absolute position encodings enter query-key pairs. Table 1 reports 1.9B vision, 0.08B adapter, 7.7B language and 9.6B total parameters.

steps.name: Expose visual information to language
steps.detail: The adapter compresses features to 256 positions between and . The language initialization is an intermediate Qwen-7B checkpoint, not its final release. A larger patch grid therefore does not directly lengthen the compressed visual sequence.

steps.name: Serialize spatial tasks
steps.detail: Coordinates are normalized into [0,1000) and tokenized as text inside <box> delimiters; <ref> marks associated descriptions. Referring grounding predicts coordinates from a phrase, while grounded captioning predicts a description given coordinates. OCR examples use <quad> for quadrilaterals.

training.text: Stage 1 freezes the LLM and trains vision plus adapter at 224×224 using text-token cross-entropy. The reported cleaned pool is 1.4B pairs, 77.3% English and 22.7% Chinese. Training processes approximately 1.5B samples over 50,000 steps with global batch 30,720.

Stage 2 trains the entire model at 448×448. Captioning, VQA, grounded captions, referring grounding, grounded captioning, OCR and pure-text autoregression share the text objective. Table 3 includes 24.8M OCR and 7.8M pure-text samples. Same-task examples are packed into sequences of length 2048.

Stage 3 yields Qwen-VL-Chat from 350k instruction examples mixing multimodal and pure-text dialogue. Vision is frozen; adapter and LLM train. ChatML marks turns, image-order strings distinguish pictures, and supervision covers answers and special tokens rather than role names or questions.
Table 8 specifies AdamW and bfloat16; stages 2/3 run 19k/8k steps with global batches 4096/128. Peak learning rates across stages are 2×10⁻⁴, 5×10⁻⁵ and 10⁻⁵, with cosine decay.

inference.text: Images pass through the encoder and adapter before language generation. Caption evaluation uses greedy decoding with the printed prompt “Descripe the image in English:”. VQAv2, OKVQA, GQA and VizWiz use open-ended greedy answers; ScienceQA instead selects the highest-confidence allowed option.

Few-shot examples are randomly sampled, without RICES retrieval. SEED-Bench video questions use four sampled frames. These are comprehension evaluations; no future-image rollout, action decoder or executed control loop is specified.

equations.explanation: Appendix E.2 gives the patch-grid sequence lengths: 224 and 448 are image side lengths in pixels, and 14 is the patch stride. The chosen adapter still outputs 256 features at either resolution.
Section 2.2 represents a box by its top-left and bottom-right coordinate pairs after normalization into [0,1000). The pair is serialized as text, without a new positional vocabulary.

results.setting: Karpathy-test; greedy caption generation after multi-task pre-training.
results.interpretation: A strong reported captioning result; the comparison does not match training data or compute.

results.task: General visual question answering on VQAv2
results.interpretation: The reported generalist gain does not surpass the listed specialist.

results.setting: Validation split; evaluated Qwen-VL and its SFT variant.
results.interpretation: Supports text-reading capability; TextVQA also appears in multi-task training, so this is not an unseen-dataset claim.

results.metric: ANLS, higher is better; paper's reported scale
results.interpretation: A clear exception to universal generalist superiority.

results.setting: Test-B; predict a target region from its description.
results.interpretation: Shows localization rather than action execution; the supplied benchmark summary does not specify its geometric acceptance threshold.

results.setting: English and Chinese benchmark evaluations of Qwen-VL-Chat.
results.metric: GPT-4 Score, higher is better; not a percentage
results.interpretation: The compared language coverage is sparse; these aggregate judged scores are not physical task-success rates.

results.task: Window versus global attention training cost
results.setting: Appendix E.3 resolution/attention ablation; hardware and batch configuration not specified for timings.
results.metric: Seconds per training iteration, lower is faster
results.comparison: Figure 8 shows lower loss for global attention at each matched resolution.
results.interpretation: The selected 448 global configuration trades a small timing penalty for lower loss. Cross-resolution speed differences are much larger; downstream accuracy is not ablated.

results.setting: Table 11; exact split and prompting/shot protocol unspecified.
results.interpretation: Improvement is relative to the actual intermediate initialization. Its CMMLU baseline is missing, and no universal preservation claim follows.

limitations.text: The query-count experiment uses ViT-L/14 at 224×224 and smoothed training-loss curves. It motivates 256 queries, but does not isolate their downstream benefit in the final ViT-bigG model or ablate positional encoding.
Cross-model results lack matched data/compute and uncertainty estimates. SFT improves some columns but lowers others; Figure 4 also does not show uniformly increasing few-shot performance.
The conclusion leaves speech/video integration, higher resolution and image/speech generation to future work. Four-frame video question answering does not establish a predictive dynamics model.

reproduction.text: Reconstruction requires the intermediate Qwen checkpoint, OpenCLIP initialization, private corpus components, task mixture and Table 8 schedule. The paper supplies optimizer/parallelism settings but no GPU model/count, software versions or complete data-release specification.

Appendix A documents cleaning categories, greedy removal of recursive grounding labels, and synthetic OCR construction. Numeric aspect-ratio, size, CLIP-score and text-length thresholds remain unstated. Appendix E.1 calls stage 1 one epoch; exact reconciliation with rounded pool/processed-sample totals is unavailable.

reasoning.text: The foundational Language & VLM backbones classification is supported. A vision encoder, adapter and language generator perform perception and grounding. Joint multimodal training supplies neither joint future/action prediction nor inverse dynamics, so the catalog's architecture, prediction-paradigm and quadrant fields remain Not applicable.

discussionQuestions: Would query counts selected by training loss remain optimal for small-text reading and grounding at fixed compute?
Does pure-text mixing preserve capabilities beyond the few benchmarks and intermediate checkpoint reported here?

evidence.location: PDF pp. 1–3, Abstract and Section 1
evidence.detail: Motivates multilingual, multi-image, fine-grained visual understanding beyond coarse descriptions; distinguishes Qwen-VL from instruction-tuned Qwen-VL-Chat.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 3–4, Section 2.1, Table 1 and Figure 3
evidence.detail: OpenCLIP ViT-bigG with stride 14; randomly initialized single-layer cross-attention; 256 learned-query outputs; 2D absolute query-key positions; 9.6B reported total parameters.

evidence.location: PDF p. 4, Section 2.2
evidence.detail: Image feature delimiters; boxes normalized within [0,1000), represented as two coordinate pairs and tokenized as text; box and reference delimiters associate regions and descriptions.

evidence.location: PDF p. 5, Section 3.1 and Table 2
evidence.detail: 5B original and 1.4B cleaned pairs; English/Chinese shares 77.3%/22.7%; frozen LLM, trainable vision/adapter, 224 resolution, text cross-entropy, about 1.5B processed samples.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 5–6, Section 3.2 and Table 3
evidence.detail: Seven tasks; 448 resolution; all modules train; 2048-token same-task packing. Captioning 19.7M, VQA 3.6M, grounding 3.5M, referring/grounded-caption tasks 8.7M each, OCR 24.8M, text 7.8M; TextVQA is listed.

evidence.location: PDF p. 6, Section 3.3 and evaluation preamble; p. 4, Figure 3
evidence.detail: 350k instruction data; mix multimodal and text dialogue; freeze visual encoder, update adapter/LLM; Qwen-VL denotes stage 2 and Qwen-VL-Chat stage 3.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 18–19, Appendix B.1–B.2 and colored format boxes
evidence.detail: Black prefixes are not supervised, blue target labels are; grounding and inverse description examples; quadrilateral OCR labels; Picture id and ChatML turns; answer/special-token SFT supervision.

evidence.location: PDF p. 20, Appendix C and Table 8
evidence.detail: AdamW, bfloat16, cosine schedule; step/batch/LR settings for all stages; optimizer sharding, no activation checkpointing, model parallelism 2 in stages 2/3. No GPU model/count or software versions appear.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Table 4, Flickr30K/VQAv2 and other columns; Section 4.1
evidence.detail: Flickr30K: Qwen-VL 85.8, Chat 81.0, InstructBLIP 82.8, Flamingo-80B 67.2. VQAv2: 79.5/78.2, Shikra-13B 77.36, PALI-X 86.1. Specifies greedy captions/answers and constrained ScienceQA choices.

evidence.detail: TextVQA 63.8/61.5 vs InstructBLIP 50.7 and DocOwl 52.6. DocVQA 65.1/62.6 vs Pix2Struct 76.6 and DocOwl 62.2. ChartQA 65.7/66.3, AI2D 62.3/57.7, OCR-VQA 75.7/70.5.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 7–8, Section 4.3 and Table 6
evidence.detail: RefCOCO test-B Qwen-VL 85.34, Chat 84.51, Shikra-13B 81.81, UNINEXT-H 91.46. GRIT Qwen-VL 78.22 vs Unified-IO 78.61; Chat entry absent.

evidence.location: PDF p. 8, Section 4.4 and Figure 4

evidence.detail: Lists image/text/CLIP filtering without numeric thresholds, longest-caption selection, maximum-confidence VQAv2 answer selection, recursive grounding cleanup, PDF/HTML render-and-text extraction filters.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 16–17, Appendix A.4 and Figure 5
evidence.detail: SynthDoG-style synthetic OCR uses COCO train2017/unlabeled2017 backgrounds, 41 English and 11 Chinese fonts and quadrilateral labels; document renderings add OCR supervision.

evidence.location: PDF p. 21, Appendix E.1 and Figure 6
evidence.detail: Reports one epoch, declining training loss and fluctuating improvement on captioning and zero-shot VQAv2; no VQA data in stage 1.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 21–22, Appendix E.2 and Figure 7
evidence.detail: ViT-L/14, 224 resolution and 64/144/256/400 queries; smoothed early and later loss curves. Gives patch counts 256 and 1024 and chooses 256 queries for final training.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 22–23, Appendix E.3, Table 10 and Figure 8
evidence.detail: Window attention uses 224-sized windows in most layers with occasional global attention. At 448, global/window speed is 10/9 s per iteration; at 896, 60/25. Figure 8 compares training loss; authors select 448 global attention.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 23–24, Appendix E.4 and Table 11
evidence.detail: Intermediate Qwen-7B initialization is distinct from final release. MMLU/C-Eval: intermediate 49.9/48.5, Qwen-VL 50.7/51.1, final Qwen-7B 58.2/63.5; intermediate CMMLU missing. Authors attribute retention to mixed pure-text data.

evidence.location: PDF p. 10, Section 6
evidence.detail: Future directions include more modalities, higher resolution/model/data scale and image/speech generation.
